Meanwhile those sets stay non-allocatable (s2_allocatableSlots requires usefulCnt.isSaturateNegative, Ittage.scala:296).

notes: Sub-case 'pulse in the same cycle as resetFinish' HOLDS: when(resetUsefulCnt) has priority over .elsewhen(resetFinish) (IttageTable.scala:185-189), so needReset stays 1; the chisel3.util.Counter value wraps to 0 in the resetFinish cycle (setsPerBank is 128/256, power of two; library semantics, not in-tree), so the next cycle starts a full sweep at set 0. That timing is reachable: the tick-saturating update at cycle C makes tickCnt=255 at C+1, updateResetUsefulCnt=1 at C+1, table pulse at C+2 where update.valid=RegNext(updateMask at C+1) and req.fire may both be 0 while resetSet===setsPerBank-1. The pulse itself cannot be dropped: it sets needReset unconditionally and is one cycle wide (tickCnt.resetZero at Ittage.scala:397 overrides selfUpdate at :379 by last-connect, so 0->255 needs >=255 further increments). The only failing state class is 'pulse while needReset=1 and resetSet=k>0': the request is coalesced into the in-flight sweep and the portion 0..k-1 is silently dropped. Sweep stall under load is the enabler (usefulCanReset needs both no read and no update in the same cycle, IttageTable.scala:182), and the same load (dense mispredicted indirects without allocatable slots) is what drives tickCnt to 255 again. Whether this counts as a violation depends on R-ITTAGE-5 demanding a full sweep per saturation; the coalescing idiom is likely intentional, but the claim text ('the request is not forgotten') is false for the 0..k-1 portion.
